bead.title: harness: CI gate — cassette presence + freshness + credentialed drift detector
bead.description:
Two CI gates lock in the contract:

(a) Cassette-as-test-fixture freshness (every PR): every harness with a TUI model surface (codex, claude, gemini, opencode, pi) has testdata/model_surface/ checked in and CapturedAt within a configured TTL (default 30 days). Stale fixtures fail because they no longer prove the parser works against current TUI output.

(b) Live-discovery drift detector (scheduled / credentialed, harness_integration tag): runs ReadXModelDiscoveryViaPTY against the live authenticated CLI, captures a fresh snapshot, diffs against the checked-in cassette. Mismatch fails with a re-record instruction. Missing credentials emit a structured SKIP (parsable by CI). SKIPs older than TTL fail the presence check above.

This is now scoped correctly: at runtime, live PTY is authoritative and uncached cassette has no role. The CI gates here exist to keep test fixtures honest, not to gate runtime behaviour.
bead.acceptance:
1) A unit test (internal/harnesses/cassette_presence_test.go or similar) asserts every harness in {codex, claude, gemini, opencode, pi} has a testdata/model_surface/ cassette and that CapturedAt is within the configured TTL; runs by default in go test ./... .
2) A harness_integration-tagged test runs against the live authenticated CLI, captures a fresh snapshot, and diffs against the cassette; mismatches fail with actionable re-record instructions.
3) CI reports SKIP vs FAIL distinctly for the credentialed drift job; SKIPs older than TTL fail the presence test.
4) Documentation explains how to re-record a cassette (and explicitly notes cassettes are test fixtures, not runtime fallbacks).
